newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Sumitomo not active in South Korean copper trade.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo not active in South Korean copper trade.

text.p: Japan's Sumitomo Corp has not been active in the South Korean copper market this year because its offers have not been as competitive as those of Chilean copper producing giant Codelco Corp, traders said on Tuesday.
"In Seoul, we have good copper suppliers such as Glencore and Codelco. Whenever we need to buy physical, we can get much more attractive prices directly from them," one trader said.
"I heard South Korea bought around 70 percent of its total copper imports from Chilean Codelco this year," he added.
An official with copper buyer LG Cable and Machinery Ltd said the company had last made spot purchases from Sumitomo in 1993 and 1994.

Toyota Tsusho Corp, the only Japanese supplier active in the South Korean market, has provided an average of 1,000 tonnes a month of refined copper to domestic end-users this year, a trader with a local trading house said.
Officials at Sumitomo's Seoul office were not immediately available for comment.
